references.text: The law to wait three years before harvesting fruit from newly planted trees, and that the fruit is only permitted in the fifth year. This explains the term 'chillel' (to make available for common use) used in Deuteronomy 20:6.
The preceding verse about a man who has built a new house and not dedicated it. The same principle of exemption from military service to enjoy the fruits of one's labor.
The following verse about a man who has become engaged to a woman. The same pattern of exemption from war to complete important life events.
A curse describing the opposite scenario: another man shall enjoy the vineyard you have planted. This verse uses the same language and theme as a warning.
Isaiah's promise of the messianic time when people will enjoy the fruit of their vineyards and their labor, without others taking it from them.
Amos's warning that the people shall plant vineyards but not drink the wine, as a judgment against Israel. The same theme of losing the fruit of one's labor.
Zephaniah's prophecy that they shall plant vineyards but not drink the wine, as part of the Lord's judgment on Judah.
